items.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: after that I was working with a big band that worked all of the society functions, Morris Allen, who still has a big band now today

ctx.x: I was too young to know it was a lot of work. I mean you know when I started doing the songs of the day at that time, was “Bet You By Golly Wow” and all that kind of stuff, I didn’t know that was a lot of work. So what I did was I hired a singer, a female singer, who, she sang half of the show and I played the other half. And it was odd because I

never missed a piano player at that time. But later on when I started, after that I was working with a big band that worked all of the society functions, Morris Allen, who still has a big band now today, and through that I started really getting, I always liked big band music, and when I was in Memphis I also played clarinet. Because I wanted to play trumpet but they didn’t have a trumpet then so the only thing they had left was the clarinet so I played the clarinet so I could be in the band, in the junior high…

You know I wanted to ask you a question, a couple of things here because you’ve got this marvelous mix and a lot of players I find have this mix. And it doesn’t get talked about that much in jazz history books, but you know, a lot of the jazz historians want to treat jazz as if it’s just jazz. But when I’ve talked to so many players, particularly to African American players that said, wait a minute, I got church background. I heard Gospel music when I was a kid, you know? Just give us an example of how the sound…
